title: Farnese Hercules Bodybuilding Program (Ancient Greek Herculean Physique Workout)
summary: NH presents a free five-day upper/lower/upper/lower/arms program modelled on the Farnese Hercules statue, which he insists is achievable naturally. The program aims for an X-taper with thick obliques, legs, posterior chain, upper back, forearms and biceps. Nucleus overload sets for forearms, calves, neck and abs, marked with Greek symbols, are appended to supersets, and the program is meant for lifters with high work capacity.
claims: The Farnese Hercules physique is achievable naturally, contrary to commenters who claim it needs drugs

The statue's strong points are well-developed obliques, massive but not lean legs, a thick posterior chain and glutes, a thick upper back without a wide lat flare, and big forearms and biceps; shoulders and triceps are less developed
The goal is a Herculean X-taper with thickness, an ancient bear mode, rather than a V-taper
Greek symbols mark nucleus overload cycles appended to supersets: Σ forearms, Φ calves, Ψ neck, Π abs, so these boring muscles cost no time and cannot be skipped
The program mixes hard sets with NO for these muscles instead of using only NO
The split is upper, lower, upper, lower, arms on five consecutive days and then a rest day; it is really a muscle split, not a true upper/lower
The program needs high work capacity and recovery; novices and many early intermediates cannot run it and should pick another program
Experienced lifters can adjust reps, sets and NO placement, but most NO sets should go to calves and the fewest to abs, since abs already get intense sets
Straight sets of abs in the program are taken to failure
The supersets are needed because the weekly workload would otherwise make sessions take four hours
Squat frequency over a career matters more than weekly volume: squatting twice a week for five years beats five times a week for one year, and daily squatting gives strength more than size
The statue's legs are big but not striated, because it shows a natural man carrying body fat in his legs
He wishes he could do farmer's walks but cannot; if squats leave you too tired, swap them for shrugs or farmer's holds
Calf raises 3x15 are the only hard calf set of the week; added up, the calf NO sets exceed what a typical hard-set routine would give
Pullovers are so good he expects to put them in every program: they build lats, chest and long-head triceps and help thoracic mobility and shoulder health
Upright rows are safe for the shoulder if you know how to do them
The idea that heavy deadlifts, good mornings, squats or rows thicken the waist is mostly nonsense, and the Farnese Hercules has a big waist anyway
Do sternum pull-ups with fat grips to target the mid back rather than the lats and add forearm work
Exercises are ordered by importance; if you must skip, cut the bottom ones, never the top
Arm day should be the least taxing day with the least tonnage, mostly isolation with a few compounds, but still relevant work rather than a pump fest
The physique will take more than two years; the statue shows a man in his prime who trained for a long time

Upper 1: bench or dips or weighted push-ups 3-4x6-12 + inverted rows AMRAP (Φ); OHP or DB press 3x6-10 + weighted chin-ups 3x5 + Russian twists 3x12-15 (Φ); skull crushers 4x8-12 + DB curls 4x6-12 + finger curls 4x8-10 (Ψ)

Lower 1: squats or Zercher squats 3-4x6-10 (Σ); RDLs or back hyperextensions 4x8-12 + shrugs 4x12-15 or farmer's walks (Π); Bulgarian split squats or single-leg press 3x10-15 + towel or DB hold 3x15 s + calf raises 3x15 (Ψ)

Upper 2: DB, barbell or seal row 3-4x6-12 + push-ups AMRAP (Π); pullovers 3x6-12 + preacher curls 3x6-10 + lateral or Arnold raises 3x8-12 (Σ); hang snatch pulls or upright rows 4x10-15 + neck curls 4x15-20 + windshield wipers 4x12-15 (Σ)

Lower 2: deadlifts 3x3-5 or good mornings 3x6-12 (Φ); block pulls 4x6-12 or farmer's walks or hip thrusts 4x10-15 + sternum pull-ups AMRAP (Π); belt squats or leg press 4x8-15 + wide-grip shrugs 4x12-15 + leg curls or GHR 4x10-20 (Φ)

Arms: close-grip bench or landmine press 4x6-10 + Kroc rows 4x6-12 or supinated rows AMRAP (Φ); hammer or pinwheel curls 4x8-12 + pullovers 4x12-15 or pull-ups AMRAP + DB flies 4x10-15 (Ψ); supinated finger curls 3x6-12 + rope triceps extensions 3x10-15 + V-sit-ups AMRAP (Ψ)
exercises: the program's one vertical pull, since the statue has blocky, not flared, lats
